rubric: evaluation/tactical-frontier-1/rubric.json (weights and anchors committed before these scores)

G: splittable ground operators in 50 of 50 scenarios
L: per the live rules each half keeps the full ammunition and acts independently; offset by weaker shots and stacked-target modifiers
O: type, sub_type and blood of the seat's own operators; the deployment stage is observed
I: the deployment stage only; play-stage selection untouched
M: deployment-split actions, engine acceptance and the new operators are visible in records and step captures
R: 314 is documented but by design absent from valid_actions; acceptance, control of the new operators and the stacking limit unverified on 4.1.0
P: 16 of 16 frozen scenario sides, every game

G: infantry and infantry fighting vehicles in 47 of 50 scenarios
L: objective defence and mobility for infantry: a local advantage
O: own units; embark and disembark are listed
I: changes play-stage selection of infantry and carriers
M: time to objective and survival need the step capture
R: documented and listed; suppression and timing rules
P: infantry in 6 of 8 frozen scenarios, but embark or disembark listed in under 1% of play decisions

G: loitering munitions in 42 and UAV in 30 of 50 scenarios; every unit observes
L: an enabler: its value appears through other decisions
O: a belief over partially observed enemies
I: a belief state that other behaviours must read
M: discovery and coverage need a new observer and a model
P: reconnaissance assets in at least 6 of 8 frozen scenarios

L: brings an idle weapon system into play; limited by dispersion and target knowledge
O: fire at visible or recently seen enemies
I: only artillery acts differently; baseline-v2 leaves it idle
M: plans and acceptance in records; damage needs the capture's judge records
R: documented and widely listed, but target choice, dispersion, flight time and friendly fire are unknown

G: correction radar in 5 of 50 scenarios; guided fire listed once
L: useful where a guide and a guided weapon meet
I: one new behaviour for the guiding unit

L: fewer losses en route; size unknown
O: a threat estimate from visible and last-seen enemies

G: state changes listed for most archetypes in most decisions
L: concealment and march trade survival against speed
O: own units' states and legal actions
M: state transitions visible in observations and action counts

G: helicopters in 26 of 50 scenarios; mines, fortifications and air defence rare
R: rarely listed; parameters with unknown effects
P: helicopters in 3 of 8 frozen scenarios; mines or fortifications in 1

L: potentially the largest: how the whole force is used
O: own forces and objectives, with seen enemies
M: roles and assignments need a new observer
R: no new action, a large change
